statement: doc_rule_parity's own findings (uncited/dangling-citation bullets) carry a fixed sentinel RuleId ("RR-9.1") rather than the cited-but-invalid token itself, since Finding.rule_id must always be a valid RuleId and an uncited bullet has no candidate id at all. check_doc_against_registry therefore returns Result<Vec<Finding>, DecodeError> (propagating the one-time parse of the fixed literal with `?`) instead of asserting infallibility with .unwrap()/.expect(), which the workspace lints (unwrap_used/expect_used = deny) forbid crate-wide.
why: Every other RuleId construction site in this workspace (enforcer-mechanization, enforcer-coordination) uses `"RR-x.y".parse()?` inside a function already returning Result, never .unwrap()/.expect() on a literal, even when the literal is fixed and known-valid by inspection. Matching that convention avoids inventing a fake infallible-parse helper.
howToApply: When a function needs a fixed, code-literal RuleId (or any branded_string! newtype) and the crate denies unwrap_used/expect_used, make the function fallible and parse with `?`; pin the literal's validity with a one-line unit test (see doc_parity_rule_id_literal_is_valid) rather than reaching for OnceLock/LazyLock caching or #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)].

statement: The bullet parser only gates markdown list-item lines (leading `-`/`*`/`+` marker) whose body contains the standalone word must/never; a continuation line of the SAME bullet (no blank line before it, no marker) is treated as part of that bullet's text, not a second bullet. The full-parity fixture originally wrote its free-text paragraph as an unmarked continuation line directly under a `-` bullet, which the word-boundary scan still classified as its own bullet body (because extract_imperative_bullets only checks for a marker at the START of `trimmed`, and a continuation line with no marker at all is a separate iteration of the `for` loop over `source.lines()` — it does NOT get merged with the previous bullet, so it was independently scanned, found `must`/`never`, and had no `[id]`, tripping the gate). The fix was a blank line separating the bullet from the free-text paragraph.
why: This is a parser-design gotcha worth recording because the module's own doc comment says "only markdown list lines are gated" but a naive continuation-style multi-line bullet will still get scanned line-by-line and can accidentally look like an ungated paragraph is actually a second ungated bullet.
howToApply: When authoring docs/agents/**, keep each must/never bullet's citation on the SAME line as the bullet marker, and separate any free-text prose from a bullet with a blank line (or make sure the continuation line does not itself contain a bare must/never) so it is not misclassified as its own citation-less bullet.

statement: docs/agents/{rust,typescript,python,common}.md cite REAL registered RuleIds already shipped in crates/enforcer-rules/rules/*.json (RUST-ARCH-1.1, RUST-BORROW-1.1, RUST-SAFETY-COMMENT, FE-ARCH-1.3, FE-TS-1.5, PYFA-1.1, PYFA-12.1, SIZE-FILE-1.1, DEFER-1.1, OWNERSET-1.1, etc.) rather than inventing placeholder ids for the persona prose, so the doc corpus itself is genuinely citation-accurate against the live registry, not merely readable prose. The workpack's fail/pass fixtures (tests/fixtures/doc_rule_parity/**) use a separate synthetic RR-100.x id family so the oracle's own test suite stays independent of drift in the real rules/*.json catalog.
why: A persona doc that cites plausible-looking but non-existent ids would itself fail the oracle it ships alongside, defeating the point of d09 (prose pretending to be enforcement). Citing real ids from the already-mechanized crates/enforcer-rules/rules/*.json catalog keeps docs/agents/** honest without requiring the fixture tests to depend on that catalog's exact contents (which other lanes are actively growing).
howToApply: When authoring or extending docs/agents/**, grep crates/enforcer-rules/rules/*.json for a real ruleId in the relevant family before citing it; never invent a plausible-looking id for persona prose, and never point the fixture tests (which must stay deterministic) at the live catalog — keep fixtures on a dedicated synthetic id range.
